ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Place the corn seeds under conditions of 25℃, darkness, and suitable moisture for germination. Take the same number of germinating seeds at fixed times every day; dry and weigh one half directly, and cut out the endosperm from the other half, dry it and weigh it. Calculate the average dry weight of each seed; the results are shown in the figure. If only considering that the nutrients needed for seed germination come from the endosperm, answer the question according to the figure: During germination, part of the nutrients in the endosperm are transformed into the constituent substances of the seedling. What is its maximum transformation rate? (Unit: mg*seed^-1*d^-1)

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, the horizontal axis is germination time, with the unit being hours, marked as 0, 24, 48, 72, 96, 120 h; the vertical axis is dry weight, with the unit being mg·seed^-1. There are two curves in the figure: the upper curve represents the total dry weight of "germinating seeds," and the values at each time point are approximately 221.3, 205.9, 205.3, 204.2, 177.7, 172.7 mg/seed; the lower curve represents the dry weight of "endosperm," and the values at each time point are approximately 198.7, 183.8, 174.9, 161.7, 118.1, 91.1 mg/seed. Then reason: The question states that only the nutrients needed for germination are considered to come from the endosperm, so at the same time point, the dry weight of the seedling constituent substances can be represented by "total dry weight of germinating seeds − dry weight of endosperm." The seedling dry weights at each time point are respectively: at 0 h, 221.3−198.7=22.6; at 24 h, 205.9−183.8=22.1; at 48 h, 205.3−174.9=30.4; at 72 h, 204.2−161.7=42.5; at 96 h, 177.7−118.1=59.6; at 120 h, 172.7−91.1=81.6 mg/seed. The increases in seedling dry weight in adjacent 24 h intervals are approximately -0.5, 8.3, 12.1, 17.1, and 22.0 mg/seed/day, respectively. The maximum value occurs from 96 h to 120 h, which is 22.0 mg·seed^-1·d^-1.
